actuation: Vacuum and positive pressure via dual miniature diaphragm pumps and 2/1 solenoid valves
constitutive_assumptions: The gripper membrane does not make contact with the ground during the grasping phase for reasonably sized payloads.
Contact mechanics can be represented as two non-linear compression springs in parallel: Fair representing the air-filled membrane and Flmp representing the lumped stiffness of the jammed assembly.
The non-linear springs act purely in compression, modeled using a ramp function H(y) = 0 for y < 0 and H(y) = y for y > 0.
The lumped elastic force Flmp is independent of test peg diameter because the jammed membrane shape remains unchanged during contact.
Normalized free volume beta follows first-order exponential dynamics analogous to a vacuum chamber pump-down.
Uniaxial shrinkage and free length xa map linearly with normalized free volume beta: xa = xu_a * beta, with maximum travel xu_a = 40.8 mm.
Elastic force Fair of the inflated membrane follows a power-law relationship with penetration depth x and peg diameter D: Fair(x, D) = 102.87 * D * x^1.88.
Lumped elastic force Flmp follows a power-law relationship with penetration depth: Flmp(x) = 25119.75 * x^1.29.
The jammed granular material causes the gripper-payload assembly to behave akin to a single rigid body.
control_variables: Membrane dimensions: nominal diameter 80 mm, height 60 mm, wall thickness 0.6 mm, encompassing volume 0.2 L, mass 18 g without filler
Base membrane elastomer material: Trollfactory Type 23 silicone rubber (Shore hardness 10 A, 600% elongation at break)
Granular filler type: Expanded Polystyrene (EPS) beads (1 mm to 4 mm diameter, bulk density 17 g/L)
Proportional control gain (Kp = 6) for sled velocity force tracking on the linear test jig
Test peg diameter for activation force and deadener benchmark tests (40 mm)
Pressure switching trigger thresholds: lower trigger Pmin = -21 kPa and upper trigger Pmax = 0.5 kPa
Contact detection force threshold on the UAV (Fm >= 5 N) to disable xy position control
Aerial dummy payload total mass (210 g) and approximate diameter (40 mm)
Nominal activation force during deadener benchmark test series (350 gf)
Benchmark repetitions (8 trials per activation force test series, 6 trials per deadener series, 6 good engagements per aerial shape)
dependent_variables: Elastic contact force of inflated membrane Fair (N)
Lumped elastic force of jammed assembly Flmp (N)
Total aerial grasp success chance (engagement chance * holding chance)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: A universal jamming gripper can attain its maximum holding force with a substantially reduced activation force (250 gf / 2.5 N) by utilizing lower granular fill ratios (66% compared to 90%).

Mixing a deadener additive (up to 15% by weight) into the silicone membrane enhances maximum holding force by up to 52% (from 10.1 N to 15.4 N) through increased membrane softness, conformability, and surface friction.

The uniaxial contact behavior of a transitioning universal jamming gripper can be modeled as two parallel non-linear compression springs representing the air-filled membrane and the jammed structure using power-law force-displacement relations.

A universal jamming gripper attached to a multicopter in a claw configuration can perform dual duty as landing gear, providing passive compliance to absorb landing shocks and eliminating the need for dedicated landing gear.

Aerial grasping success with a soft jamming gripper is strongly shape-dependent, excelling on geometries with vertical faces (cube, ridge) but suffering from slippage on spherical surfaces and complete failure on wedging geometries (pyramid).

experimental_setup: Benchtop linear test jig comprising a 12 V power supply, a belt-driven linear rail driven by a stepper motor with a 3D printer board, holding the gripper assembly above fixed cylindrical test pegs (30 mm to 50 mm diameter) without interlocking features
Proportional force controller (Kp = 6) executing linear sled velocity adjustments to track nominal activation force during the evacuation phase
Integrated gripper instrumentation consisting of a custom STM32L1 MCU board, MEMS differential pressure sensor, and load cell for internal force and pressure logging

Aerial testbed comprising a modified AscTec Firefly hexacopter (430 mm wheelbase, 1 kg payload capacity) carrying a Raspberry Pi 4 companion computer, Pixhawk autopilot, and bottom-mounted TRIGGER in a claw configuration
Laboratory motion-capture system providing 6-DOF tracking and an adaptive super-twisting descent controller providing <= 3 cm horizontal position accuracy
Eight synthetic 3D-printed payload shapes (cube, ridge, cake, hollow cylinder, tube, ball, triangle, pyramid) mounted on a weighted 210 g test container
future_work: Developing an active force controller to track nominal activation force during the evacuation phase in flight to remove the human operator from the loop
Implementing trajectory optimization to guide the UAV to the payload while accounting for universal jamming gripper dynamics
Assessing membrane durability and the long-term degradation of deadener-induced stickiness over time
Investigating alternative membrane morphologies (such as cup-shaped or multi-chambered geometries) to prevent lateral slippage and gravity-induced granular settling
Exploring the addition of internal and external geometric features on cast silicone membranes
Fabricating structural components from carbon fiber composites to achieve further weight reductions
independent_variables: Granular fill ratio (66% and 90% EPS infill)
Nominal activation force (150 gf to 650 gf)
Deadener additive concentration in silicone membrane (0%, 5%, 10%, 15% by weight)
Test peg / payload diameter (30 mm, 40 mm, 50 mm)
Payload geometry / shape (cube, ridge, cake, hollow cylinder, tube, ball, triangle, pyramid)
limitations_inferred: The multi-second evacuation cycle time leaves the hovering aerial platform vulnerable to external wind disturbances and ground effect drift while waiting for particle jamming to complete.
Relying primarily on friction and surface adhesion without geometric interlocking makes holding performance sensitive to surface contamination, dust accumulation, and moisture.
The thin 0.6 mm silicone membrane may present limited puncture and abrasion resistance when interacting with sharp or abrasive real-world payloads.
Disabling horizontal position control upon contact requires the aircraft to rely entirely on contact friction, which could lead to dislocation on inclined or low-friction surfaces.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Stickiness imparted by the deadener additive is temporary and degrades over time due to silicone aging and dust/dirt accumulation, requiring a clean environment or periodic membrane replacement.

The current design is constrained to grasping objects from the floor in a claw configuration; horizontal grasping leads to gravity-induced particle accumulation and requires payloads to resist lateral pushing forces.
Miniature low-power pumps result in longer cycle times (11 s vs 4 s in high-power setups) and a lower vacuum pressure differential (approx. 28 kPa vs >80 kPa in stationary systems).
The bag-shaped membrane generates horizontal reaction forces that cause slippage on rounded or slanted shapes (such as spheres and tubes).
Grasping fails on wedging geometries (pyramids) and shapes with insufficient contact surface area (triangles).
Engagement chance was the primary limiting factor in aerial trials, heavily affected by positioning accuracy and human operator timing.
Activation force was not actively regulated during free-flight aerial grasping experiments.
Estimating payload size via contact force curves requires highly precise position measurements that may not be available in practical field settings.
main_results: TRIGGER achieved 10.1 N of holding force with an unmodified membrane and 15.4 N with 15% deadener on a 40 mm cylindrical peg lacking geometric interlocking, requiring an activation force of only 250 gf (2.5 N).
Lower membrane fill ratios (66% vs 90%) significantly lowered the activation force required to achieve maximum holding force (250 gf for 66% infill vs 650 gf for 90% infill).
Incorporating 15% deadener additive into the silicone formulation increased holding force by 52% due to increased softness, greater contact surface area, and higher friction.
The complete gripper assembly achieved a lightweight mass of 380 g and operated under 10 W of electrical power, reaching a vacuum differential of approximately 28 kPa.

Aerial pick-and-place and synthetic shape experiments achieved over 85% total success chance on shapes with vertical faces (cube, ridge) and over 55% on cake, hollow cylinder, and tube shapes, while spherical shapes had 30% success, triangles had 14%, and pyramids could not be lifted.
TRIGGER successfully functioned as the landing gear for the hexacopter, providing passive compliance that absorbed touchdown impact forces.
modeling_methods: Non-linear regression analysis identifying power-law force-displacement relationships for the inflated membrane Fair(x, D) and jammed lumped structure Flmp(x)
Uniaxial contact force model combining two parallel compression springs with ramp functions enforcing compression-only contact Fug = Fair(H(x), D) + Flmp(H(x - xa))
First-order transfer function in the Laplace s-domain modeling normalized free volume dynamics beta(s) = R(s) / (1 + sT) with time constant T derived from evacuation duration
Linear kinematic mapping between normalized free volume beta and uniaxial free length / membrane shrinkage xa = xu_a * beta
Prismatic joint contact and disk simulation model for rigid-body robotics simulators (Gazebo) incorporating state transitions governed by beta
Discrete state classification kgr(beta) separating gripper states into closed/jammed (beta <= 1%), opened/fluidized (beta >= 99%), and in transition
performance_metrics: Holding force to mass ratio Fh/m (N/kg)
Minimum activation force Fa (gf or N)
possible_gap_implications: Demonstrates that a low-power, lightweight pneumatic architecture (sub-10 W, 380 g) can generate sufficient vacuum (28 kPa) and holding force (15 N) for aerial manipulation, bridging the gap between heavy stationary laboratory jamming setups and payload-constrained aerial platforms.

Shows that adjusting granular fill ratios and membrane chemical additives can decouple holding strength from high activation forces, enabling jamming grippers to be deployed on fragile, floating, or underactuated systems.
Identifies that bag-type jamming membranes produce lateral reaction forces that cause floating aerial platforms to dislocate, pointing to the need for cup-shaped or patterned membrane architectures.
paper.research_objective: Design, fabricate, model, and experimentally validate a lightweight, modular, omnidirectional universal jamming gripper (TRIGGER) tailored for aerial grasping and landing gear duty on multirotor UAVs, which operates with low activation force and low power consumption.
paper.research_problem: Aerial manipulation requires physical interaction with surroundings, but multirotor UAVs face severe limitations including constrained payload capacity, limited attachment space, underactuated dynamics, dynamic coupling, and position errors from ground effects. Existing aerial grippers (rigid jaw grippers, pneumatic soft fingers) suffer from high mass, manufacturing complexity, high operating pressure requirements (100–250 kPa) requiring heavy pumps or CO2 canisters, lack of omnidirectionality, sensitivity to approach angles, and inability to double as landing gear.
paper.title: TRIGGER: A Lightweight Universal Jamming Gripper for Aerial Grasping
